words.gloss: he who has subdued or extinguished the desires of the five senses

literal: The power of him who extinguished the five, the king of those in the wide heaven, Indra himself, is sufficient proof.
translation: Indra, the king of the dwellers of the vast heavens, is himself sufficient proof of the great power of the one who has conquered all five senses.
modern: ஐந்து புலன்களையும் அடக்கியவனுடைய ஆற்றலுக்கு, அகன்ற வானுலகில் வாழ்பவர்களின் தலைவனாகிய இந்திரனே போதுமான சான்றாவான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the immense spiritual power of a person who has completely subdued their five senses. The poet uses the word 'அவித்தான்' (one who extinguished) to compare sensory desires to a raging fire that must be put out. To prove the magnitude of this achievement, the poet points to Indra, the king of the gods in the vast heavens, as a sufficient witness ('கரி'). Indra's own traditional stories serve as a testament to the consequences of failing to control the senses, thereby proving the supreme strength of those who successfully do so.
